results.finding: Opens on a puzzling scenario (two buyers, one jacket), states the claim, places the chapter in Eva's order and gives a specific roadmap; none of the weak patterns.

Opens with a callback, then sorts findings by how settled they are, gives questions, closes the part and hands off; the established bullets summarise body findings rather than add new evidence, and the part close is the spec's declared synthesis, not a new subtopic.

p50a states what no single section states (one counted fact, one writer per claim, one place deriving, one commit; 'None of this needs a faster copy') and the so-what that the decision can be made before any product is bought; p54a-p54b give the part synthesis (one problem, three-part remedy, no platform replaced) and the list the reader can write, starting with stock.

p50a returns to 'the web shopper and the store customer of the opening' and says what decides who gets the jacket; p54a returns to the part opening's product page with description, price and stock badge changing at different speeds.

The intro reader predicted every roadmap item in order (Oversell; numbers; moment of promise; locations and channels; service with writers, interaction needs, events vs copies; four options, trade-offs, stages; worked Oversell; failures; count checked against a study) and the evidence (the Oversell, vendor documentation, one inventory-accuracy study), matching AC-4's expected.
Reader answered 4 (10 - 3 - 1 - 2) and named it available-to-promise, a derived figure, as expected.

Reader named several writers, scheduled copying, snapshot overwrite, the commit window, no buffer, no reconciliation and a wrong count; said a five-minute interval shrinks but does not remove the causes, and gave the remedy (one writer per state, events, per-channel buffers in one service, atomic commit, reconciliation), as expected.

Reader said only checkout at order creation must ask the service and wait with an atomic commit, and that the listing badge, add to cart, marketplace push and click-and-collect may read a slightly stale copy, as expected.
